summary: Design and compare columnar ingestion, partition, rollup, and query layouts from representative workload, lineage, late-data, and measurement evidence.
triggers: An analytical workload needs partition, sort, compression, or rollup design.
Query layouts must be compared using representative data and repeatable measurements.
Late-arriving events, backfills, or rollup corrections need an explicit path.
antiTriggers: Install or migrate a production database without a separate authorized operation.
Choose partitions without cardinality, retention, and query evidence.
Infer production cost or capacity from toy data.

provenance.note: Method source read in full and independently rewritten for portable product use; the historical file remains unchanged.
Workload, lineage, late-data, measurement, and termination semantics informed the rewrite; no source prose was copied.
Ownership and evidence boundaries were consulted; no layout performance or migration result is asserted.
